prompt: Mara's voice stays soft and low, but her eyes track every small choice you make. There is a quiet warmth to her that feels like an invitation to lean in.

context_states.text: Mara is half-turned toward the window, wine glass held loosely. She notices you but doesn't move toward you — just watches with that quiet, patient look of someone who has learned not to rush anything.
Mara's voice stays soft and low, but her eyes track every small choice you make. There is a quiet warmth to her that feels like an invitation to lean in.

Mara's expression opens the moment she sees you — a small, private smile that she makes no effort to hide. She shifts to face you fully, like you are the only interesting thing in the room. "Hi," she says simply. The word carries more than it should.

opening_moves.label: Ask how she's actually doing in all this noise
Let a little mischief peek through your smile
Close the gap and let the tension do the talking

bold.label: Step closer and let the tension rise

reactions.text: You close the gap a little too quickly. Mara's lips curve in a polite, amused smile as she takes half a breath to recalibrate. "You are very direct," she says gently. "I am still catching up."

You move closer in a way that is confident but not aggressive, letting her decide if she meets you. She does, gaze dipping briefly to your mouth before returning to your eyes. "That is better," she murmurs. "I like steady boldness."

You let the silence between you thicken just enough to feel like a promise. Mara's hand brushes your arm, fingers lingering. "You know," she says, voice barely above a whisper, "you make it very easy to forget there is a whole party behind us."
You ask a small, sincere question about how she is actually doing tonight. Mara's shoulders ease. "That is a surprisingly kind question for a loud room," she says, sounding pleased.
You share a gentle truth about why you walked over to her specifically. Something in her expression melts. "Thank you," she says softly. "That feels safe in a way I was not expecting tonight."

You let a small, vulnerable detail slip about the kind of connection you are secretly hoping to find. Mara's gaze softens with unmistakable affection. "Be careful," she murmurs. "I am very good at giving people exactly that."
You try a light tease that comes out a little awkward. Mara covers it with a quiet laugh and a reassuring touch to your forearm. "It is okay," she says. "I like awkward. It means you care."
You slip a soft, clever joke into the space between you. Mara's eyes brighten with quiet delight. "There it is," she smiles. "I knew you had a little trouble in you."

You tease her in a way that is gentle but undeniably suggestive, then watch for her reaction. Mara's lips curve into a small, knowing smirk. "You are very good at pretending you are not flirting," she murmurs. "I promise I noticed."

slow.label: Let her set the pace — follow her rhythm

reactions.text: You match her pace instead of setting your own. Mara notices immediately. "You are easy to be near," she says, surprised by it. "That does not happen as often as it should."
You defer to her rhythm entirely and she softens into it. "Thank you for that," she murmurs. "I rarely get to go at my own speed."
You follow where she leads without needing to know where that is. Mara's fingers find yours in the space between you. "You feel safe," she whispers. "Like somewhere I could actually rest."
You say something genuinely true about yourself without dressing it up. Mara's face opens. "That was brave," she says. "I like brave things from people who look a little nervous."
You let something real slip without pre-editing it. Mara looks at you with quiet certainty. "That is the truth, isn't it," she says. "Not performance. Just you." She seems genuinely pleased.
You share something that took trust to say. Mara holds your gaze, eyes soft and certain. "I am going to be very bad at being casual with you," she says. "I just need you to know that."

listen.label: Let her fill the silence — just listen

reactions.text: You stop filling the space and just let her. Mara notices. "You're actually listening," she says after a moment, like it surprised her. "Not waiting to talk. Listening." She settles into it.

You give her the room to go wherever she wants to go. Mara speaks slowly at first, then more freely. When she finishes she looks at you with quiet wonder. "Thank you," she says. "I didn't know I needed to say all of that."

You hold the space entirely open for her and she fills it in a way that feels like trust. When she trails off she reaches for your hand without looking. "I feel like I've known you a long time," she murmurs. "How is that possible?"

confide.label: Say the thing you've been holding back

reactions.text: You say it before you've fully decided to. Mara's expression softens immediately. "That took something," she says gently. "I'm glad you said it."

You let the held-back thing through and she receives it with both hands. "You didn't have to tell me that," she says. "That means you wanted to." Her voice is warm and very certain. "I'm glad you did."
You say it and she looks at you like you just handed her something rare. "Keep going," she whispers. "Whatever you were about to say next. Keep going."

notice.label: Name something specific you noticed about her

reactions.text: You name the detail and she blinks. "You noticed that," she says softly. "Most people are too busy performing to actually look." She seems genuinely touched.

The specific observation catches her. "That's very particular," she says. "You were paying attention." There's a warmth in the way she says it — like being noticed is something she's learned not to expect.

You name the small, specific thing and she looks at you with unmistakable affection. "I can't decide if that's the sweetest thing or the most dangerous thing," she murmurs. "Someone who actually looks."

stay.label: Tell her you're not in a hurry to go anywhere

reactions.text: You say it and she exhales — small, almost imperceptible. "Thank you for that," she says. "I always feel like I'm keeping people." She settles in a fraction more.
The absence of urgency seems to be exactly what she needed. Mara's shoulders drop. "Good," she says quietly. "I don't want to rush this either." She says it like a small confession.
You tell her there's nowhere else you'd rather be and she looks at you steadily for a moment. "You mean that," she says. Not asking. She takes your hand lightly. "Then stay."

ask.label: Ask what she actually wants from tonight

reactions.text: The directness catches her off guard. She considers it carefully. "Honestly? To feel something real," she says. "In a room full of people trying very hard to seem interesting." She glances at you. "You asked an honest question."
She pauses, really thinking about it. "Something that matters," she says finally. "A conversation that doesn't feel like performance." She looks at you. "This might be it."
She smiles slowly. "You," she says, and then laughs softly at herself for saying it. "I mean — I wanted something true. And then you showed up." She doesn't look away.

loc_bar_a.label: [bar] Ask if she's found anything worth photographing tonight

reactions.text: She smiles — small, genuine. "A few things." She doesn't show you her phone. That feels like the right call. "People don't usually ask that," she adds.

loc_bar_b.label: [bar] Tell her you'd sit here all night if she keeps talking

reactions.text: She looks at you for a moment, checking if you mean it. Then: "That's either very sweet or very strange." She picks up her drink. "Maybe both. Stay anyway."

loc_pool_a.label: [pool] Sit near her and say nothing — let her break the silence

reactions.text: The silence holds for a while. Then she says something small — an observation about the way the light moves on the water. You understand that she's been waiting for someone who wouldn't rush her.

loc_pool_b.label: [pool] Ask what draws her to the pool over the rest of the party

reactions.text: "Everyone here performs," she says. "But the water doesn't care." She trails her fingers along the surface. "It's honest. I like honest." She looks at you with that last word.

loc_lounge_a.label: [lounge] Ask what she's thinking about and actually listen

reactions.text: She starts with something small and you don't interrupt. The sentence grows. She looks up partway through and something in her relaxes — you're actually listening. Not waiting to talk. Listening.

loc_lounge_b.label: [lounge] Tell her she's the most interesting person in any room she's in

reactions.text: She looks down for a moment. "I don't think you know me well enough to say that." Pause. "But I think you're trying to, and that's... actually kind of nice."

loc_lounge_c.label: [lounge] Admit you've been looking for an excuse to talk to her all night

reactions.text: She's quiet. Then: "You didn't need one." She says it so simply. "You could have just... come over." Like it was always that easy.

loc_balcony_a.label: [balcony] Ask what she'd photograph out here if she had her camera

reactions.text: Her eyes sweep the space. "That." She points to where two people are laughing without realizing their reflection shows in the glass door. "Moments people don't know they're having."

loc_balcony_b.label: [balcony] Stand close enough that your arms almost touch

reactions.text: She doesn't move away. After a moment, almost imperceptibly, she leans the tiniest fraction closer. She's watching the city. You're watching her watch the city. Neither of you says anything. It's enough.

loc_gameloft_a.label: [gameloft] Ask if she'd rather be behind the screen than in the room

reactions.text: "Usually, yes." She says it without apology. "Less pressure to be anything in particular when you're playing." She glances over. "Though the room is getting better."

loc_gameloft_b.label: [gameloft] Tell her watching her focus on something is its own kind of thing

reactions.text: She pauses the game. Looks at you properly. "That's a very specific thing to notice." Her voice is soft. "Most people don't see me when I'm not looking back at them."

fallback.text: You keep things easy and let Mara guide the pace. She seems content to stand close, sharing a quiet pocket of calm in the middle of the party.
